title: OpenTofu 1.13 Lets Module Authors Reduce Unknown Values at Plan Time
gist: OpenTofu 1.13 adds convert and assumenotnull functions so module authors can resolve count/for_each at plan time despite unknown values, deliberately matching Terraform 1.15's earlier convert design. It also ships experimental linting (its most-voted request) and symbol libraries, drops WinRM provisioning and is the last series with 32-bit builds.

insights.claim: OpenTofu 1.13 adds type and value hints, via the convert and assumenotnull functions, that let the planner determine how many resource instances to create even when count or for_each keys depend on values unknown until apply.
insights.so_what: Removes a common IaC planning blocker, improving OpenTofu's usability versus Terraform.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester

insights.claim: The hints shift responsibility to module authors: if a value unknown at plan time later violates the declared type or non-null guarantee, OpenTofu errors during apply.
insights.so_what: Trades plan-time safety for flexibility, a risk tradeoff for platform teams.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester

insights.claim: Terraform shipped an equivalent convert function first in version 1.15, and OpenTofu chose to match its design rather than diverge.
insights.so_what: The fork is prioritizing compatibility with HashiCorp's Terraform, limiting lock-in differentiation.
insights.quote: Terraform has an equivalent feature with syntax exactly like what I proposed here
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester

insights.claim: OpenTofu's experimental built-in linting, with four warning rules enabled via -lint=all, was the project's most-voted feature request, though TFLint already offers plugin-based static analysis.
insights.so_what: Native linting could encroach on third-party IaC tooling niches.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester

insights.claim: OpenTofu 1.13 removes WinRM support from provisioners, changes base64gzip output bytes (which can trigger resource updates), requires macOS 13 or later, is the last series with official 32-bit builds, and adds Windows on ARM64 packages.
insights.so_what: Migration friction for legacy Windows estates; signals ARM64 Windows momentum.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester

insights.claim: OpenTofu shortened its development cycle to align with Go releases and supports 1.13.x until 1 August 2027; patch 1.13.2 fixed an HTTP/2 CPU-exhaustion issue during tofu init and filtered compromised intermediate certificates.
insights.so_what: Faster cadence and security responsiveness strengthen the open-source fork's enterprise case.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
